subject: Inference ops scorecard & next-test workshop
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Cicely Ortega <cicely@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Inference ops scorecard & next-test workshop

Hi Cicely — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps below (attaching the one-page scorecard and the demo recording):

Summary (from today's call)
- Primary goal: find an inference platform that gives predictable p95 latency for short-chat use cases and transparent per-route cost visibility.
- Key constraints: procurement timeline (~Q1 renewal window), on-prem evaluation for IP-sensitive workloads, SOC 2 evidence.
- Baseline hyperscaler comparisons discussed: you wanted a small, focused set of experiments rather than a full bake-off.

Redwood differentiators we highlighted (concise)
- Smart routing + pinned model variants: keep SLAs during fallback without changing API surface.
- Prefix/KV caching: reduces token cost for repeated prompts with warm prefixes (real gains on our customer chat workloads).
- Per-route observability: token-level cost + latency breakdowns in the Console and an exportable trace for your SREs.
- Dedicated pools & reserved capacity: predictable throughput for enterprise workloads.

Proposed tactical test plan (1-hour workshop + 48hr runs)
1) Latency profile: 1k short prompts (8-32 tokens output), measure p50/p95/p99 and cold vs warmed KV cache.
2) Long-context streaming: 50 long prompts (10k context) to validate memory/KV behavior and streaming tail latency.
3) Cost delta: run the same traffic on Redwood hosted (and a Dedicated config) vs your hyperscaler API with same model family to compare $/1M tokens after batching.
4) Observability check: validate that per-route panel shows requests, token breakdown, and sample traces; capture a trace to share with your SREs.

Asks from you
- Confirm which metrics matter most (we can prioritize p95 vs p99, token-cost, or SLA violations).
- Provide a rough sample of daily request volume and the most common prompt size.
- Confirm whether procurement wants an initial pricing range for Dedicated vs hosted before the workshop.

Next steps
- If that plan looks good I’ll schedule a 60–75 minute workshop the week of Dec 13 to run the tests and hand over traces & dashboards.
- Marissa will demo the Console's per-route telemetry and share a sample trace export.
- Sergio will prepare a Dedicated pricing ballpark and a procurement checklist (SOC 2 / contract steps).

Attachments: redwood-infer-ops-scorecard.xlsx (one-pager), demo-recording-20261206.mp4, SOC2-summary.pdf

Thanks — short items below if you want to pick a date now.

— Diego

Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 15:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Inference ops scorecard & next-test workshop

Thanks Diego — this is super helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Priority metrics: p95 latency (short-chat/prompt) and cost per 1M tokens are our top two. p99 is nice-to-have but not gating for the first pass.
2) Volume: roughly 250k requests/day today for our chat product; median output ~28 tokens, tail out to ~512 tokens occasionally.
3) On-prem evaluation: yes, we need the option to validate the Private (VPC/on-prem) flow — our security team will want a brief readout of network topology and KMS integration.
4) SOC2: please include the SOC2 summary (you attached — thanks). Our procurement lead (cc'd) wants a rough Dedicated estimate to help with internal approvals.

Procurement note: our procurement cycles usually request an initial SOW/estimate before scheduling technical workshops — can you provide a ballpark monthly committed price for a Dedicated pool sized for 100k requests/day with burst? If you can give a conservative and an aggressive estimate that would help.

If you can send the estimates this week we can loop legal/procurement and lock a workshop date for week of Dec 13. Also please send the Console trace export example so our SREs can confirm it maps to their observability workflow (we use Datadog + internal tracing pipeline).

On the SOC2 — can you confirm whether audit logs include per-request identifiers and retention windows?

Best,
Cicely Ortega
Head of Platform, Acme Robotics
cicely@acme-robotics.com

Internal note / action items based on Cicely's reply: 

Marissa — please prepare a ~10 min Console demo clip that:
- Shows per-route latency and token-cost panels, export a trace (zip) that includes request id and sample spans.
- Include a short note on how the trace can be pushed to Datadog or S3 (we have both sample scripts).
- Tie the demo to the planned tests (latency short + long-context).

Sergio — pricing/procurement:
- Please draft two Dedicated ballpark options (conservative and aggressive) sized for ~100k req/day baseline with 2x burst. Include estimated committed monthly cost, and call-out any discounts for annual/enterprise licensing.
- Prepare a one-page procurement checklist: SOC 2 evidence, KMS/HSM options, contract SLAs, support tiers, and estimated lead times for Private deployment if they opt for that.

Risk note: Cicely mentioned on-prem evaluation and Datadog. Confirm that our trace export has request IDs that map to their SRE ingestion (we usually include a request_id and parent_span). Also check model runtime compatibility with A100 class GPUs (their ops lead signaled A100s in infra).

I'll follow up with Acme procurement and propose Dec 14 or Dec 15 for the 75-min workshop depending on their availability.

— Diego
